The formulation as written matches the commonly cited PACELC wording, but that is not evidence under prompt 04. Kind is history, so this does not block approval by itself.

PG 17 19.6.2: commits wait 'until their WAL records are replicated to num_sync synchronous standbys' - the named ones.

issues.text: Carried from round 1. Claim 1 (PACELC formulation) is unverified: versions.yaml has no standards key for CAP/PACELC, so no permitted source exists. Not a blocker (kind history); stays unverified until the owner adds a key (meta open_questions asks for this).
issues.quote: a classic extension of the CAP theorem
issues.fix: Owner: add a standards key for the PACELC formulation to content/versions.yaml, then re-run review 04 on claim 1. No lesson text change needed.

issues.text: New in changed text. The prose says the normal-running column has the product list reading the latest value from the primary, then two sentences later says the list may move because 'its row accepts slightly old data'. I paused: does the row choose latest or accept old? Only the earlier 'only because no other copy exists yet' reconciles it, two paragraphs up.
issues.quote: in the second, the product list and viewing your own order both read the latest value from the primary today.
issues.fix: Add 'only because no other copy exists yet, while its row accepts slightly old data' after 'the product list' in that sentence, or drop the list from it.

issues.text: New in changed text. The synchronous-replication paragraph now covers commit waiting, losing db's data, receive vs apply, the lab's wait and an out-of-scope setting in five sentences; I read it twice, and 'Which of the two' made me look back to find which two.
issues.quote: Which of the two a commit waits for is a setting outside this lesson.
issues.fix: Split the paragraph before 'A replica first receives a change', and write 'Whether a commit waits for the receive or the apply is a setting outside this lesson.'
